summary: Round 5, production pass. NO FINDINGS. (1) THE OVERRIDE'S THIRD CONDITION HOLDS FOR THIS ROUND AND IS CHECKED AGAINST THE BYTES: the only src/main hunk with any executable content in the whole staged diff outside what round 4 passed is GrantIssuer.java, and both of its hunks are inside /** */ blocks -- no statement, no signature, no import changed. Every executable line round 4 quoted is present verbatim: the mint hoisted above both loops in deliver (SubscriptionHub.java:568-570), `sinks -> { }` for the DIRECT arm (452-453), coldMode's `asked == INLINE ? PROXY : asked` (474), `new SegmentDelivery(Long.MAX_VALUE, false, consumers, false)` (471), both Push compact-constructor guards (99-106), mintGrant's null-issuer guard and UncheckedIOException wrap (499-516), AssemblingSubscriber's seven-argument rebuild carrying push.grant() (65-66), and DefaultIngest's `config.directEnabled() ? new GrantIssuer(store) : null` (247). STATED AS CORROBORATION, NOT PROOF, and the override says the same: .harness/review stores verdicts and not diffs, so the round-4 bytes are not recoverable and the claim 'SubscriptionHub.java is byte-identical to the bytes round 4 reviewed' cannot be bound by anything in the tree. The override's headline ('no round since the cap changed any production logic') reaches one round further back than its own evidence ('since the round-3 verdicts'), which leaves the round-2 -> round-3 fix unevidenced; the signed condition is per-round ('this round changes no production logic') and that one holds, and rounds 2 and 3's own verdicts record only prose minors on the production side, so nothing contradicts the wider phrasing either. (2) THE NEW PROSE IS TRUE WHERE IT IS CHECKABLE. GrantIssuer's rewritten opening: IngestConfig.directEnabled (IngestConfig.java:70) and FetchPolicyConfig.directEnabled (FetchPolicyConfig.java:50) both exist; DefaultIngest constructs the issuer once per pod under that flag (DefaultIngest.java:247) and the refusal is in the constructor (GrantIssuer.java:120) plus an explicit conditional requirePresignedUrls at DefaultIngest.java:223-224, so 'the refusal happens when the pod is built, not when a consumer first asks' is exact. grantFor's new paragraph: deliver does hoist the mint above both loops, and 'the API does not resist it' is still true -- grantFor mints fresh per call. The backlog cell's checkable claims hold: SubscriptionHub is at 700 lines, M5.65 resolves to a new row, CanPresign counts signings (StoreFakes.java:292,305), LogCapture exists with all three channels documented and exactly two callers (GrantNeverLoggedTest, DirectServingTest), and Grant.toString and SignedUrl.toString both redact so no production path puts a URL in a message. (3) COST, unchanged since round 4 and re-derived from source rather than from the cell: one presign per SEGMENT per publish, minted before either loop, so the signing rate is flat in segments and in pods and flat in both consumers and runs -- not shards-per-node. The DIRECT arm's Source is a no-op lambda, so the serving side buys no GET, no stat and no list; coldMode adds none either. ConsumerClient is the only subscribe() call site in any src/main and takes one RunKey, which is what makes the hoist the right fix rather than a coincidence of one test's grouping. (4) AUDIT TRAIL: all eight staged review/verdicts/M5.45d/*.json are byte-identical to the .harness/review artifacts their own diff_sha256 names, so the after-the-fact check the standing authority relies on is on faithful copies. (5) OPERATIONAL NOTE, NOT A FINDING AND NOT ABOUT THE STAGED BYTES: the working tree was being mutated while this review ran (an unstaged SubscriptionHub leak probe present at one point, an unstaged StoreFakes edit later), which is consistent with the test pass measuring in parallel and is also why `scripts/review.sh context` reported check-module FAILED with a Gradle in-progress-results NoSuchFileException. Nothing unstaged reaches the commit, but the commit should be made from a tree whose unstaged edits have been restored -- confirm `git status` is clean apart from the staged set before committing.
